lines: Clock generator with three eight-step gate sequencers driven by it
Sets the tempo of the internal clock, 15 to 3840 BPM
Joins the three tracks into one 24-step sequence at 1x24, where only the T1 output carries pulses, or runs them as three independent eight-step tracks at 3x8
Restarts every track from its first step
Starts and stops the clock; while it is stopped the clock output and all three track outputs stay at 0V
Sets how many of the eight steps that track plays, 0 to 8; at 0 that track's output stays at 0V
Turns that step of the track on or off; an active step sends a pulse from its track output when the sequencer reaches it
Clocks all three tracks from an external source, and stops the internal clock while a cable is patched
A rising edge above 1V restarts every track from its first step
A 10V gate lasting half of each clock period, at 0V while the clock is stopped
Carries a 10V pulse, half a clock period long, when an active step of track 1 comes round; in 1x24 mode it carries the pulses of all 24 steps
Carries a 10V pulse, half a clock period long, when an active step of track 2 comes round, and stays at 0V in 1x24 mode
Carries a 10V pulse, half a clock period long, when an active step of track 3 comes round, and stays at 0V in 1x24 mode
Clockkky.notes: Clock tempo is 2^v * 60 BPM over a -2 to 6 knob range, default 120 BPM. Track outputs and the clock output are gated by the same half-period window, so a track pulse is half a clock period long. In 1x24 mode the three tracks run one after another and only T1 outputs.

lines: Random sequence generator built from five planets orbiting one another around a central star, whose coordinates become control voltages
Sets the starting angle of that planet on its orbit, -180 to 180 degrees
Sets the distance from that planet to the one before it in the chain, 1 to 30
Sets how fast that planet turns, -180 to 180 degrees per second, orbiting the other way below zero
Puts every planet back at its starting angle
Multiplies the X coordinate of both selected planets before it reaches the X1 and X2 outputs, 0 to 3 times
Multiplies the Y coordinate of both selected planets before it reaches the Y1 and Y2 outputs, 0 to 3 times
Chooses which of the five planets feeds the X1 and Y1 outputs
Chooses which of the five planets feeds the X2 and Y2 outputs
Makes the X1 and X2 outputs carry the absolute value of the X coordinate, so they never fall below 0V
Makes the Y1 and Y2 outputs carry the absolute value of the Y coordinate, so they never fall below 0V
A rising edge above 1V puts every planet back at its starting angle
The X coordinate of the planet chosen for the first output pair, one tenth of its value multiplied by the X scale knob
The Y coordinate of the planet chosen for the first output pair, one tenth of its value multiplied by the Y scale knob
The X coordinate of the planet chosen for the second output pair, one tenth of its value multiplied by the X scale knob
The Y coordinate of the planet chosen for the second output pair, one tenth of its value multiplied by the Y scale knob
Planetz.notes: Planet positions are chained: each planet orbits the previous one, the first orbiting a fixed star at the origin. Output voltage is coordinate/10 times the scale knob, so with rays at maximum it can reach well beyond 10V. Angles advance 100 times a second by speed/100 degrees.

lines: Deterministic pseudo-random sequence generator in which a frog jumps around sixteen stones, each holding a jump value and a note of the chosen scale
Lit, a jump onto the same note as the one before produces no trigger
Sets the initial jump value of that stone, 0 to 15, the number of stones the frog moves on from it; in PRG mode it sets that stone's note, 0 for silence, 1 for C, 2 for C sharp and on up
PRG walks the stones in order on an internal 120 BPM clock and hands the jump knobs over to editing the notes of the current scale; RUN plays the jumping sequence
Sets the base note of the scale as a MIDI note number, 21 to 96, with 60 putting the first note of the scale at 0V
Puts the frog on the first stone and refills every stone with the jump value set by its knob
Chooses one of four scales: C ionian, A aeolian, a pentatonic up and down, or E phrygian up and down
Sets how many stones the frog uses, 1 to 16; in PRG mode it picks which of three octaves the jump knobs write into
Lit, the trigger output rests at 10V and drops to 0V for 1ms at each note, which the maker's tooltip calls gate mode; unlit it rests at 0V and pulses to 10V
Each rising edge makes the frog jump and play the note of the stone it lands on
A rising edge above 1V puts the frog on the first stone and refills every stone with the jump value set by its knob
Adds its voltage, rounded to whole volts, to the scale chosen by the SCALE knob, one scale per volt, wrapping round the four scales
The pitch of the note being played, 1V per octave
A 1ms 10V pulse at each note played, which the button below it inverts into a 1ms drop from 10V
Note — In RUN mode the frog moves only on a rising edge at the CLK input, so with nothing patched there nothing is played
MusiFrog.notes: The CLK input is ignored in PRG mode, where an internal 2Hz clock steps the stones. Each visit to a stone raises that stone's jump value by one, so the sequence evolves until reset. The scale CV is only read in RUN mode. Edited scales are saved with the patch.

lines: Synthesiser voice modelled on the Buchla Music Easel, with a five-step sequencer, an envelope, a pulser, a noise source, a modulator, a wavefolding oscillator, two gates, a delay and an inverter
Sets the pitch of the oscillator and of the modulator at 1V per octave, and is read only by whichever of them has its KEYB switch on
A rising edge above 1V is the keyboard trigger, which can start the envelope, the pulser, the sequencer and the noise hold; held high it sustains the envelope in Sust mode
Clocks the synth from an external source and stops the internal clock while a cable is patched
Sets the tempo of the internal clock, 15 to 3840 BPM
Chooses what advances the sequencer: each clock tick, each pulse from the pulser, or each keyboard trigger
Sets the sequence to three, four or five steps
Sets the voltage that step sends to the SEQ output, 0-10V
Turned on, reaching that step fires a sequencer trigger, which can start the envelope, the pulser or the noise hold
The voltage of the step the sequencer is on, held until it moves on
Chooses what starts the envelope: a keyboard trigger, a pulse from the pulser, or a sequencer trigger; Self mode ignores this switch
Sust holds the envelope at full while the GATE input stays high, Trans runs it through whatever the gate does, and Self restarts the envelope as soon as it ends
Sets how long the envelope takes to rise to 10V, 1ms to 5 seconds
Sets how long the envelope holds at 10V before it falls, 1ms to 5 seconds
Sets how long the envelope takes to fall from 10V back to 0V, 1ms to 5 seconds
The envelope, 0-10V
Chooses what starts the pulser: a keyboard trigger, a clock tick, or a sequencer trigger; Self mode ignores this switch
Trig starts the pulser from the source its TRIG switch names; Self restarts the pulser as soon as it ends
Sets how long the pulser takes to fall, 1ms to 5 seconds, after a fixed 5ms rise
Attenuates the voltage at the pulser modulation input, which lengthens the pulser period
Lengthens the pulser period, scaled by the pulser MODUL knob
The pulser envelope
Chooses what makes the noise section draw new random values: a keyboard trigger, a pulse from the pulser, or a sequencer trigger
A random voltage between 0V and 10V, held until the noise section is triggered again
A random voltage between 0V and 1V, held until the noise section is triggered again
Adds the voltage at the V/Oct input to the modulator frequency
Rounds the modulator frequency down to whole semitones
Chooses the modulator waveform: saw, square or triangle
Hi runs the modulator from 11.3Hz to 1760Hz across its frequency slider, Lo from 0.17Hz to 55Hz
Tunes the modulator by up to three semitones either way
Chooses what the modulator does to the oscillator: FM on its pitch, AM on its level, or nothing at Off
Sets the modulator frequency, 11.3Hz to 1760Hz in the Hi range and 0.17Hz to 55Hz in the Lo range
Attenuates the voltage at the modulator frequency input, which shifts the modulator an octave per volt with this slider at the top
Shifts the modulator frequency an octave per volt, scaled by the modulator frequency modulation slider
Sets how strongly the modulator is applied to the oscillator, and scales the MOD output by the same amount
Attenuates the voltage at the modulation amount input, which adds to the strength of the modulation applied to the oscillator
Adds to the strength of the modulation applied to the oscillator, scaled by the modulation amount slider
The modulator waveform scaled by the MODUL amount slider, so it carries nothing with that slider down
Adds the voltage at the V/Oct input to the oscillator pitch
Rounds the oscillator pitch down to whole semitones
Blends the sine wave of the oscillator with the wave chosen by the oscillator WAVE switch
Inverts the pitch modulation, so a rising voltage lowers the pitch
Tunes the oscillator by up to three semitones either way
Chooses the wave blended with the sine: saw, square or triangle
Sets the oscillator pitch, 11.3Hz to 1760Hz
Attenuates the voltage at the pitch modulation input, which shifts the oscillator an octave per volt with this slider at the top
Shifts the oscillator pitch an octave per volt, scaled by the pitch modulation slider
Sets how hard the oscillator waveform is folded, adding harmonics as it rises
Attenuates the voltage at the timbre modulation input, which adds to the folding of the oscillator waveform
Adds to the folding of the oscillator waveform, scaled by the timbre modulation slider
Chooses what Gate 1 does with the oscillator: a VCA, a lowpass filter, or both mixed equally
Chooses what Gate 2 does with its source: a VCA, a lowpass filter, or both mixed equally
Chooses what Gate 2 takes in: the preamp, the modulator, or the inverted output of Gate 1
Chooses what the preamp carries: the noise generator, the EXT input, or nothing at Off
The external signal the preamp carries when the PREMP switch is at Ext
Sets the gain of Gate 1 as a VCA and the cutoff of its lowpass filter, reaching 8192Hz at the top
Attenuates the voltage at the Gate 1 modulation input, which adds to the Gate 1 level
Adds to the level of Gate 1, scaled by the Gate 1 modulation slider
Sets the gain of Gate 2 as a VCA and the cutoff of its lowpass filter, reaching 8192Hz at the top
Attenuates the voltage at the Gate 2 modulation input, which adds to the Gate 2 level
Adds to the level of Gate 2, scaled by the Gate 2 modulation slider
Sets how much of Gate 1 goes into the mix, from silence to twice its level
Sets how much of Gate 2 goes into the mix, from silence to twice its level
Sets the delay time, 5ms to 1500ms, and the maker's tooltip calls it reverb time
Lengthens the delay by 100ms per volt
Sets how much of the delayed signal is fed back into the delay, 0 to 100%
Sets the balance between the dry mix and the delayed signal, all dry at 0% and all delay at 100%
Sets the level of the OUT jack, from silence to twice the mixed signal
The mixed and delayed voice at the level set by VOL
The signal that the INV output turns upside down
The voltage at the INVERT input with its sign flipped
Note — To play it, patch a 1V per octave signal to the V/Oct input and a gate to the GATE input; the maker's quick start names those two connections and the gate is what makes the keyboard trigger
Zefiro.notes: The README says the modulator covers 11Hz to 55Hz; the code gives 0.17Hz to 55Hz in the Lo range and 11.3Hz to 1760Hz in the Hi range, and the frequency tooltip reads in Hz for the Hi range only, so it is wrong in Lo. The maker's tooltips name the delay section reverb while the panel prints only TIME, FBACK and WET, and the README calls it a delay. The preamp's Off position is PREAMPSRC_FEEDBACK in the source, a feedback path that is not implemented and returns silence. The Gate 2 level is not clamped before use because of a typo that clamps the Gate 1 variable instead, so Gate 2 modulation can push its level past the slider range; Gate 1 has already been computed by then, so nothing else is disturbed. The INVERT input and the MOD output have no family: the inverter carries whatever is patched into it, and the modulator output is an LFO or an audio-rate wave according to its RANGE switch.

lines: Three independent sample and hold sections sharing one twelve-note quantizer
Lit, the voltage sampled by that section is snapped to a note of the scale at 1V per octave
Chooses how a sample becomes a note: Prop spreads the active notes evenly across each volt, Nearest takes the closest active note, Clamp takes one only within half a semitone and else holds
Adds that note to the scale used by all three sections, or takes it out; the last remaining note cannot be switched off
A rising edge samples the voltage at the IN jack of that section; with nothing patched here that section never samples
The voltage that section samples when its HOLD input receives a rising edge; with nothing patched a fresh random voltage between 0V and 1V is sampled instead
The voltage that section has held since its last sample, limited to -5V to 5V
Rests at 10V and drops to 0V for 1ms whenever a sample changes the held voltage, staying at 10V when the new sample repeats the old one
Note — A section samples only while a cable is in its HOLD input; with that jack empty its output holds whatever it last had and never changes
HoldMeTight.notes: Sampling happens only while the HOLD input is patched: an unpatched HOLD jack leaves that section's output frozen. The output family is cv rather than pitch because quantizing is off until its button is lit.

lines: Cyclic cellular automaton drawn on the panel and read out as two control voltages, where a cell steps to the next state when a neighbour already holds that state
Sets how many states a cell can take, 2 to 26, the last wrapping back to the first
Sets the width of a cell in pixels, 1 to 6; changing it refills the grid with random states
Sets how often the grid is evolved, 0 to 31, one step per drawn frame at 31; at 0 the grid stops evolving
Sets the size of the random block dropped onto the grid, 1 to 50 percent of the grid height
Makes that random block a diamond or a square
Picks one of the four cells compared against each cell, as a position in the seven by seven square around it, 0 to 48; 24 is the cell itself and the four defaults give its nearest four neighbours
Replaces the next colour in the state palette with one built from the hue, saturation and lightness inputs
Drops a block of cells in random states onto the grid at a random position
Refills the whole grid with random states
Replaces one of the four neighbour positions with a random one
Sets the hue of the next sampled colour, the voltage divided by ten with its sign dropped; a random hue is used when nothing is patched
Sets the saturation of the next sampled colour, the voltage divided by ten with its sign dropped; a random saturation is used when nothing is patched
Sets the lightness of the next sampled colour, the voltage divided by ten with its sign dropped; a random lightness is used when nothing is patched
A rising edge replaces the next colour in the state palette with one built from the hue, saturation and lightness inputs
A rising edge drops a block of cells in random states onto the grid at a random position
A rising edge replaces one of the four neighbour positions with a random one
A rising edge refills the whole grid with random states
The average state of the cells down the upper half of a vertical line one third across the grid, scaled to -2V to 2V
The average state of the cells down the upper half of a vertical line two thirds across the grid, scaled to -2V to 2V
Note — The grid is evolved from the panel drawing, so it stops evolving whenever the module is scrolled out of view or the window is hidden, and the outputs hold their last value
Note — At a SPEED of 0 the grid stops evolving and the outputs hold their last value
CyclicCA.notes: The README says the outputs average a whole vertical line; the code sums only the top half of each line, over a height of caheight/2. The grid is evolved from inside the display widget's draw call, so evolution stops when the module is not being drawn. The automaton grid itself is one display widget with no clickable controls.

lines: Note generator that adds one of two numbers to a running value at each clock and picks a note by counting the 1s in that value written in a chosen base
Sets the high part of the starting value, 0 to 63, each step worth 64; moving it reloads the running value from the start value
Sets the low part of the starting value, 0 to 63; moving it reloads the running value from the start value
Sets the high part of addend A, 0 to 63, each step worth 64
Sets the low part of addend A, 0 to 63
Sets the high part of addend B, 0 to 63, each step worth 64
Sets the low part of addend B, 0 to 63
Sets how often addend B is added in place of addend A, never at 0 and always at 1
Sets the base the running value is written in before its 1s are counted, 1 to 10; at 1 the running value itself becomes the note index
Sets how many notes the scale runs to, 1 to 24, repeating the chosen notes an octave higher once they run out
Chooses when a note is played: 1 at every clock pulse, 2 only when the note differs from the one before, 3 only when it repeats the one before
Shifts the played note by -24 to 24 semitones, or by that many notes of the scale when the REL button is lit
Makes the offset count notes of the scale rather than semitones
Appends the scale in reverse, so the sequence turns round at the top instead of dropping back
Puts the running value back to the start value
Adds that note to the scale or takes it out; the last remaining note cannot be switched off
Each rising edge adds one of the two addends to the running value and plays the note that follows from it
Adds to the offset knob at 1V per octave, a twelfth of a volt per semitone, the total held to -24 to 24 semitones
Adds a tenth of its voltage to the probability knob, so 10V alone always picks addend B
A rising edge above 1V puts the running value back to the start value
Rests at 10V and drops to 0V for 1ms at each note played
The pitch of the note being played, 1V per octave, limited to -5V to 5V
Note — A note is played only on a rising edge at the CLK input, so with nothing patched there the outputs never change
MusiMath.notes: The maker's tooltips call the paired Start, Add A and Add B knobs high and low nibbles, though each covers 0 to 63. The algorithm follows Lars Kindermann's MusiNum. The offset input is read as 1V/oct and rounded to semitones after the knob is added.
